Fit a distribution-preserving surrogate to a simulation ensemble

Source: R/surrogate.R
fit_surrogate.Rd

Trains an emulator mapping the ensemble's parameter sets (ensemble$params, the design X) to its outputs (ensemble$outputs, the responses Y), so an expensive forward model can be replaced by a fast surrogate that still reports predictive uncertainty (mean + sd per output) – the property a calibration / inverse step needs preserved (contract C7, inst/surrogate_contract.md). The ensemble is ingested through C5 (as_fb_ensemble()), so any conforming producer works.

Usage

fit_surrogate(
  ensemble,
  method = NULL,
  outputs = NULL,
  n_features = 256L,
  ard = TRUE,
  ard_refit = FALSE,
  joint = TRUE,
  cov_rank = NULL,
  cov_method = "eigen",
  seed = 1L,
  ...
)

Arguments

ensemble

A C5 ensemble source (an fb_ensemble, a PESTO manifest, a list(params, outputs), or a path).

method

One of the registered methods; "rff" (default) is always available. See register_surrogate().

outputs

Optional character vector selecting output columns to emulate; NULL (default) emulates all of them.

n_features

Number of random Fourier features for method = "rff".

ard

Logical; for method = "rff", learn per-dimension (automatic relevance determination) lengthscales by maximising the model evidence (default TRUE). FALSE uses a single isotropic median-heuristic lengthscale. Vacuous with one parameter.

ard_refit

When ard = TRUE, controls the relevance objective. FALSE (default) holds the prior/noise precisions (a, t) at their isotropic-fit values. TRUE re-estimates (a, t) by evidence at each candidate lengthscale (the evidence profiled over (a, t)) – a fuller, never-lower marginal likelihood, but in-sample, so it can over-shorten lengthscales. "cv" instead maximises the held-out predictive log-density over a k-fold split, the regularised fuller-ARD: it keeps the relevance sharpening without the in-sample over-shortening.

joint

Logical; for method = "rff" with two or more outputs, fit a joint multi-output model preserving the cross-output predictive covariance (default TRUE). FALSE fits one independent model per output (marginals only). The per-output <o>_sd contract is unchanged either way; only the off-diagonal covariance (exposed by predict(..., cov = TRUE)) differs.

cov_rank

Optional integer; for a joint rff fit with k outputs, store the cross-output covariance in a rank-cov_rank factor-analysis form (U U' + diag) instead of the dense k x k, for large output counts. The per-output marginal sd and the covariance diagonal are reproduced exactly; only the off-diagonal covariance is approximated. NULL (default) or cov_rank >= k keeps the full covariance. See predict(..., cov = "lowrank") for the compact predictive return.

cov_method

How the rank-cov_rank factor is fitted (only when cov_rank is set): "eigen" (default) truncates the covariance's eigendecomposition; "fa" learns the loadings by factor-analysis EM, which recovers them more faithfully when the residual diagonal is heteroscedastic (the eigenvectors of the full covariance are otherwise contaminated by the uneven diagonal); "auto" picks "fa" or "eigen" from the heteroscedasticity of the eigen-residual diagonal. The covariance diagonal is reproduced exactly in every case. The resolved method is recorded in the fitted object.

seed

Integer RNG seed for the random features (reproducibility).

...

Passed to a registered method's fit function.

Value

An object of class c("fb_surrogate", "list") with a predict.fb_surrogate() method.

Details

The built-in method = "rff" (default) is a self-contained random-Fourier- features Bayesian linear surrogate with evidence-optimised predictive variance. By default it uses ARD lengthscales (per-input relevance learned from the evidence) and a joint multi-output fit that preserves the predictive covariance across outputs (not only the marginals) – the distribution-preserving property the calibration / inverse consumers rely on. Richer methods (kernR's CME, PESTO's GP) register via register_surrogate().

See also

predict.fb_surrogate(), register_surrogate(), as_fb_ensemble().

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- data.frame(a = runif(120, -2, 2), b = runif(120, -2, 2))
e <- fb_ensemble(
  params = x,
  outputs = data.frame(y = sin(x$a) + 0.5 * x$b^2 + rnorm(120, 0, 0.05))
)
s <- fit_surrogate(e)
predict(s, data.frame(a = 0, b = 1))
#>      y_mean       y_sd
#> y 0.5216926 0.05329176
